learning_objective: 🎯 Discover the musicality of words! Learn how to use rhythm, rhyme, and powerful imagery to express complex emotions in just a few lines.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Poetry relies on sensory details. Instead of telling the reader how you feel, you use words that appeal to the five senses (sight, sound, smell, touch, taste) to make them experience it directly.
Rhythm is the heartbeat of a poem. It is created by the pattern of stressed and unstressed syllables. Meter is the formal, mathematical measurement of this rhythm (like iambic pentameter).
Tools that bend the literal meaning of words. Similes compare using 'like' or 'as'. Metaphors state one thing *is* another. Personification gives human qualities to non-human things.
Poems are divided into lines and stanzas. You can follow strict traditional forms (like a 14-line Sonnet or a 3-line Haiku) or use Free Verse, which has no set rules for rhyme or meter.

Rhyme connects words with similar sounds, usually at the end of lines. But poets also use Alliteration (repeating starting consonant sounds, like 'wild wind') and Assonance (repeating vowel sounds) for musical effect.

fun_activity.title: ✂️ Blackout Poetry
fun_activity.instructions: Take a page from an old, unwanted newspaper or book. Take a black marker and cross out almost all the text, leaving only a few select words visible. The words left behind will form a brand new, unique poem!

exam_tips: 📌 Always identify the rhyme scheme of a given poem using letters (e.g., AABB, ABAB) when doing poetry analysis.
📌 Don't confuse Simile and Metaphor. 'He fought like a lion' is a simile. 'He was a lion in battle' is a metaphor.
📌 When writing original poetry for an assignment, Free Verse is often safer and more expressive than forcing a bad rhyme.
quick_recap: ⭐ Poetry is about economy of language; every single word must serve a purpose.
⭐ Free verse doesn't mean 'no rhythm'—it just means the rhythm mimics natural speech rather than strict metrical rules.
⭐ Imagery is the core of poetry; always aim to paint a vivid picture in the reader's mind.
